rv.q: This production is ably directed and choreographed by Kathleen Marshall, who has drawn out all the winsomeness of her cast.
A lively, competent staging of a sweet but creaky show, “Bells Are Ringing” will need all the gumption of its energetic heroine to stand out amid the season’s competitive musical roster.
Perhaps this scenic device can be taken as an metaphor for the entire, disappointing enterprise.

This revival of Bells Are Ringing truly and accurately reflects the state of popular musical theatre (back when it was called musical comedy) over 40 years ago, entertaining as a minor historical curiosity, but not much more.

cn.t: This affectionate revival of the 1950s musical offers competent staging and energetic performances, but the creaky material struggles to connect with modern audiences beyond nostalgic charm and a few lively dance numbers.

vs.sum: The Gerald Schoenfeld Theatre offers good sightlines with minimal obstructions, although some side seats may have partial views. The sound quality is generally strong, enhancing the theatrical experience. However, the seating is tight, which can affect comfort, particularly for taller patrons. The theater's ambiance is charming with its historic character, and while facilities are adequate, expect some lines at the bar and restrooms.

acc.note: 7 wheelchair spaces in Orchestra. Infrared devices available.
